description:
Public exploit code released earlier this week claims that a local Windows user can gain SYSTEM privileges through the Common Log File System driver.

title: New SignDrop Zero-Day Exploit Turns Windows CLFS Security Feature Into SYSTEM Access

description:
A search result isn't always safe. An access request isn't always harmless. And a familiar account doesn't always mean a familiar person is using it. Simple things to remember. Yet a surprising amount of this week's trouble starts right there.

title: ThreatsDay: 59 Linux Kernel Bugs, Falcon Spyware, GSocket Backdoors + 17 More Stories

description:
The ongoing campaign targeting ConnectWise ScreenConnect deployments involves the exploitation of a now-patched critical security flaw in the remote access software, and not a new vulnerability, it has emerged.

title: SCKit Malware Turns ScreenConnect Support Sessions Into Potential MSP Attack Paths

description:
Cybersecurity researchers have found that lookalike domains masquerading as artificial intelligence (AI) tools are being used to serve ClickFix-style lures, browser-hijacking malware, and a set of extensions that hijack user searches.

This delivery pattern has been codenamed TypoPrompting by Island.

title: 186 Fake AI Domains Redirect Users to ClickFix Lures, Browser Malware, and Search Hijackers

description:
Citrix has released patches for multiple critical security flaws impacting NetScaler ADC, Citrix NetScaler Gateway, and NetScaler Console that could lead to denial-of-service (DoS) or an authentication bypass.

The critical vulnerabilities that impact NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway are listed below -

title: Citrix Patches 12 NetScaler and Secure Access Client Flaws, Including Authentication Bypass

description:
A critical flaw in Red Hat Quay allows an attacker who can access a Quay registry to read and overwrite private container images in every repository.

Quay enables anonymous access by default, and while it is enabled, the attacker needs no account. When it is off, anyone with a valid account can still exploit the flaw, Red Hat said yesterday. The company has released fixed builds for eight Quay
title: Critical Red Hat Quay Flaw Lets Attackers Read and Overwrite All Private Container Images in a Registry

description:
PTC has released patches for a new critical vulnerability impacting Windchill and FlexPLM software that, if successfully exploited, could result in remote code execution.

The security flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-126325, carries a CVSS v4 score of 9.2 out of a maximum of 10.0.

It has been described as a case of improper input validation and deserialization of untrusted data that could result in
title: PTC Patches Critical Windchill and FlexPLM Flaw That Could Enable Remote Code Execution

description:
Since mid-August 2026, a phishing operation has been stealing live Google sessions from corporate users. Every check defenders normally lean on to judge a link came back clean, and the operator designed it that way on purpose.

The Threat Research team at Material Security spotted the campaign and has since taken down hundreds of attacker domains in an effort the team calls Operation CloudFire.
title: Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign

description:
N-able on Thursday said it's investigating a new public disclosure containing claims of additional vulnerabilities in on-premise versions of N-central running version 2026.4.1 HF2.

title: New N-central Exploits Work Against Patched Servers, Enable Root RCE and Windows SYSTEM Access

description:
Security teams have more alerts, logs, and monitoring tools than ever. Yet when an attack happens, one simple question can still take too long to answer: Who or what is behind this activity, and what can they access?

A suspicious login might belong to an employee. An unusual API call could come from a machine account. Or an AI agent might be accessing sensitive systems using permissions nobody
title: Webinar: See How Identity Blind Spots Put Your SOC at Risk and How to Close Them

description:
Google Cloud VMs on AMD Turin chips need a guest OS patch and a stop-and-start to protect against three CPU side-channel flaws, Google said this week.

The company has already applied mitigations against attacks between VMs, and between VMs and the host. Inside a VM, the flaws may let an attacker with code on the same processor core infer data from other processes or the kernel.

title: Google Cloud Warns Three AMD Turin CPU Flaws Could Leak Data Across Processes in VMs

description:
A critical flaw in MongoDB Server allows an unauthenticated attacker to send two requests that trigger a crash on the database server. The crash occurs only if that server is later chosen to take over as the main server while it still lacks some recent changes.

MongoDB, the company that makes the database, released fixed versions earlier this week.

The affected servers are members of a replica
title: Critical Pre-Auth MongoDB Flaw (CVE-2026-118383) Can Crash Lagging Servers on Failover

description:
A flaw fixed in Node.js this week lets unauthenticated clients crash servers that use the runtime's built-in HTTP/2 support on the 24.x and 26.x release lines. A second HTTP/2 flaw can cause a server to send a client pieces of its memory, including responses intended for other connections.

Fixed versions were released for all three supported lines: 22.23.5, 24.22.3, and 26.13.1.

title: Node.js Fixes 16 Flaws, Including HTTP/2 Bugs That Crash Servers and Leak Other Connections' Data

description:

title: Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories
